title: Staged multi-GPU communication coordinator with attention-tiling and kernel-aware scheduling
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Prefill/decode scheduling and kernel selection currently treat multi-GPU runs with coarse-grained stages: a full prefill, then full decode. With heterogeneous GPU pools and variable sequence-length distributions, this causes suboptimal kernel choices and limited overlap between NCCL collectives and compute. This ticket implements a staged communication coordinator that slices prefill into attention-tiling windows, drives kernel selection per tile, and orchestrates NCCL transfers to overlap with local kernels, improving throughput and p99 latency on heterogeneous clusters.
motivation: We frequently see wasted GPU cycles when large NCCL collectives are serialized between prefill and decode. Models with long context lengths pay heavy prefill communication costs. On mixed hardware (A100+H100 or different memory configs) a single kernel choice per entire request penalizes some devices. By breaking prefill into tiles and selecting kernels per tile + per-device, we can overlap NCCL with local compute and pick kernels tuned to the active sequence window and hardware, reducing end-to-end token cost and tail latency.
design_summary: 1) Staging: introduce 'tile' units inside prefill (e.g., 256-token tiles) where KV slices are produced and synchronized. 2) Coordinator: a multi-GPU coordinator state machine that schedules NCCL all-reduce/all-gather for each tile, attempting to launch collective comms while other devices are executing local kernel work for the next tile. 3) Kernel-aware scheduling: kernel selector exposes candidate kernels per (model, seq_len_tile, device_capability) and the coordinator picks per-device kernels with a tie-breaker that favors overlap-friendly kernels (lower comm-start variance). 4) NCCL overlap heuristics: measure per-device compute headroom and time-to-collective; prefer partial collects when beneficial and fall back to full collect when headroom low. 5) Compatibility modes: conservative mode (serial behavior) and aggressive mode (tile-level parallelism) with runtime flags and rollout gate.
implementation_plan: Add tile abstraction to prefill path and KV cache layout changes (conductor + runtime).
Extend kernel selector API to accept (tile_length, device_features) and return ranked kernels with estimated compute and comm timings.
Implement coordinator state machine that tracks per-device readiness, launches NCCL ops opportunistically, and coordinates rollback/fallback.
Add telemetry hooks: per-tile timing, NCCL overlap percentage, chosen kernel id, and fallback events.
Run microbenchmarks on homogeneous and heterogeneous 4-GPU setups (A100x4, A100+H100 mix) and tune heuristics.
Add integration tests and staged rollout via runtime-1.20 feature flag.
Document config knobs and failure modes for SRE/Support.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prefill throughput improvement >= 18% on long-context workloads (context >= 8k) on heterogeneous clusters compared to baseline.
p95/p99 generation latency reduced by >= 12% on mixed hardware runs without increasing token error rates.
NCCL overlap metric (time overlapped with compute / total NCCL time) >= 60% on target workloads in aggressive mode.
No regression in single-GPU runs and conservative mode reproduces existing behavior.
Unit and integration tests for coordinator state transitions and kernel-selector compatibility added and passing in CI.
Feature gate and rollout plan in runtime-1.20 release notes.
Telemetry dashboards (per-route) show kernel selection distributions and overlap for at least 3 customer workloads.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased code-path complexity could introduce deadlocks between compute and NCCL. Mitigation: formalize coordinator state transitions, add watchdog timeouts, and assert-based invariants in debug builds.
Risk: Aggressive tiling may increase small NCCL operations overhead. Mitigation: include adaptive tile sizing and combine-split heuristics; revert to larger tiles when measured throughput drops.

Risk: Kernel-selector estimation inaccuracies leading to poor choices on novel hardware. Mitigation: log estimated vs observed timings, auto-tune candidate scores, and provide an override list per device family.
Risk: Hardware heterogeneity edge cases (e.g., NVLink topology differences). Mitigation: topology-aware device grouping and prefer intra-node groups for full collects.
Risk: Rollout may surface flaky e2e tests. Mitigation: staged rollout behind feature flag and Canary job run against representative clusters.
Risk: Observability gaps for new per-tile metrics. Mitigation: add required metrics before enabling aggressive mode for customers.
Risk: Resource fragmentation for Dedicated customers if tile scheduling affects capacity guarantees. Mitigation: conservative mode for Dedicated with SLA constraints.
perf_targets: Target measurements on 4-GPU heterogeneous setups: tokens/sec +18% for long contexts, p99 latency -12%, GPU utilization improved by +8 percentage points, NCCL overlap >=60%. Baseline comparisons recorded in benchmark-suite/long_context_v2.
measurement_plan: 1) Microbench harness: synthetic prefills at tile sizes {128,256,512} across batch sizes {1,4,16} and two hardware mixes. 2) Real-model sweep: run Llama2-70b-like topology and measure per-route metrics for 24h. 3) Telemetry: emit per-tile events (tile_id, start_compute_ns, start_comm_ns, end_comm_ns, kernel_id) and build dashboards. 4) CI: add synthetic multi-gpu test that asserts no deadlocks and verifies overlap metrics at minimal thresholds.
notes: Prototype findings (local tests): tiling at 256 tokens allowed our smaller GPU in a mixed set to finish compute earlier and start NCCL, increasing overlap window by ~47% in early runs.
Early kernel-selector integration required small changes to kernel metadata (add expected_comm_start_stddev).
We should coordinate with infra to ensure NCCL version and cuda drivers are consistent across canary clusters.
SRE to schedule a canary on dedicated-customer-sim cluster before enabling default.
Document expected disk and memory layout changes for KV cache when tiling is enabled.
Consider a follow-up ticket for decode-side tiling if prefill gains are validated.

Related research note: compare with ENG-11902 and ENG-10321 for orchestration primitives but do not reuse their naming; this ticket is focused on tile-level kernel selection and opportunistic collectives.
